notes:
Summary: Nebula QuickServe is a realtime personalization platform (SaaS) with per-user recommendation and chat augmentation on page load. High emphasis on p95 tail latency and predictable cost. Target metrics: p95 < 40ms for short seqs (<=64 tokens), p50 ~ <10ms; sustained throughput 500-1,000 req/s per region for primary use-case. Cost sensitivity: wants to reduce per-100k-token cost vs managed API; looking for batching/caching/quantization guidance.

Technical requirements and preferences:
- Primary workloads: low-latency chat snippets (short context), fast reranking for recommendations, embeddings for KNN personalization.
- Model candidates: Llama 2 / Mistral family for cost/latency balance; fallback to distilled 7B for tail.
- Routing: need region-aware routing + fallback model variant when Dedicated pool saturated.
- Persistence & residency: must keep user personalization vectors in-region (EU and NA regions), retention 90 days.
- Security: SSO/SAML, SOC2 compliance, audit logs, KMS integration for key management. Prefer VPC peering to avoid public egress.

Optimize interest (specific asks):
- Redwood Optimize: recommendations for batching (max tokens per batch vs latency tradeoff), KV/prefix caching for repeated prefixes, quantization profiles (int8/int4) and expected perf delta.
- Perf benchmarking: requested a Redwood-provided benchmark harness that measures p50/p95/p99 for seq lengths 8/32/64/256, token generation rates, GPU utilization, and cost estimates per million tokens. Wants raw traces for us to run internal cost model.
- Quantization: run comparison of int8 vs int4 on their workload, report accuracy delta on rerank evaluation set.

POC plan and asks:
- 4-week POC on Dedicated reserved pool (2x A100 equivalent), initial lab benchmark by Redwood is required.
- Deliverables: benchmark report, config recommendations for batching/caching, suggested compilation/kernel flags, A/B test plan for fallback policy.

Quotes/feedback from call:
- "Latency is our top constraint — if p95 creeps above 40ms we drop sessions." — VP Eng
- "Need a clear ROI vs public API; show per-token cost and ops savings from caching." — Head of ML

Next steps and ownership:
- Redwood AE (Alicia) to coordinate benchmark slot and contract terms.
- SE (Marcus) to run in-lab perf and provide config knobs.
- Security (Priya) to respond to open SOC2/KMS and network peering items.

Key blockers: procurement timeline (end of quarter), detailed network/firewall requirements for VPC peering, confirm SLA for p95 tail. Urgency: high — aiming to complete POC and procurement by 2026-06.
